events.feedback: Fast Facts: Ribbon PalmScientific Name: Livistona decora (formerly known and still frequently sold as Livistona decipiens)Common Names: Ribbon Palm, Ribbon Fan Palm, Weeping Cabbage PalmOrigin: Coast of Queensland, AustraliaGrowth Rate: Fast (once established, can grow up to 12–24 inches of trunk per year)USDA Hardiness Zones: 9a–11 (Highly cold-hardy; established palms can handle short-term drops down to 20°F / -6.5°C with minimal damage)Key Features & IdentificationThe "Ribbon" Foliage: This palm gets its name from its deeply divided, costapalmate (fan-shaped) leaves. The leaf segments are split nearly to the petiole, ending in long, delicate, weeping tips that dangle downward. In a breeze, they flutter like green ribbons, giving the entire canopy a graceful, fountain-like appearance.Trunk: Solitary and slender, reaching up to 30–40 feet in cultivation (up to 60 feet in its native habitat). The trunk is smooth and greyish-brown with light, ringed scars from old leaves.Spiny Petioles:
